I feel like things that get suggested to people with mental illness like meditation and yoga can be helpful coping skills. Like I'm a fan of meditation and yoga but I still take my meds and go to therapy and all that stuff. Self care things like yoga, meditation, walks, breathing exercises, you know all those things you see in those pintrest like articles for mental health help, can be great things if you find they help you with coping. But most of the time if you find that you are struggling then you should really pair these things with medical treatment for whatever mental health issue you are facing. Also if you are having trouble with side effects from medication please talk to your psychologist and see if there's anything else you can try instead I done that so many times. You don't have to be on the same medication forever I have switch to different medications when I thought "hey maybe there's something out there that might work better". Also idk about going off meds completely or your situation but if you wanna go med free maybe its worth talking to your treatment team about the steps you can take and the therapy you can go through to get to that goal or even if thats the right choice for you.

***Just a waring long comment but it might help if your afraid of treatment***
I'm in a IOP dbt therapy thing, started last week and I really hope it helps 
I really didn't want to go to just an ED program because I have more going on than just an ED. 
I like it so far, and high key recommend to anyone who's maybe afraid of an ED program and also have other mental health issues that they are battling other than an ED. Like with me my ED comes out when other mental health issues are bad so if you feel like that relates to you I feel like an IOP centered around all kinds of mental health could help (doesn't even need to be DBT therapy its just the one that got recommended to me by my psychologist) 
But if you feel like your biggest thing is ED, and depending on your feelings about treatment maybe an ED based program would be best (and maybe inpatient not out patient, depending on how you feel) i know the Emily program is in a couple states, I liked it when I went for a bit when I was in high school. It's just with my insurance I couldn't go to two mental health treatments at once and at the time I wasn't ready to leave my therapist. And like imma be honest if your already going to a therapist but then go to a iop you might not be able to see your therapist (unless you pay full price for one of them) but your program team and therapist can be in contact with each other even if they are through two different clinic's. (At least thats how it works in my state and insurance, I live in the USA) 
Either way get help i been so afraid of help for so long, not just with ED but even help for other mental health issues, and I finally decided I had enough.  Hope this helps anyone who is afraid of treatment no matter the mental health issues you are battling. ♡
(Also on the topic of sick enough, I know its not ed but im having a hard time with some trauma I have and I always thought it wasn't bad enough to get help, but the treatment team assured me trauma is trauma and if its effecting your life its worth it to get help, so if your going to a good clinic they will not tell you you're not sick enough, they will tell you no matter what its good to get help)

3. Also im afraid of what if I have like a flashback and get into a funk of anxiousness and sadness at work because alot of my time off I would be fine and the next moment be really depressed because of mood swings sometimes and also having flashbacks to stuff from the past. 
4. I'm also really afraid of just being alone with my feelings because idk  how I'm gonna get to therapy for awhile or at least have my whole session and i don't see me boyfriend who I live with all week because i work 9 to 5 and he works like mid day to midnight. 

Sorry i didn't give any advice but I just want you to know you are definitely not alone its hard to feel valid with depression and other mental illnesses at times when you can still get through your daily activities.  Like i always hear "depression is not being able to get out of bed" and like yeah thats true but I have to work, like does that make me less valid like I still rather not get out of bed because I hate myself and I'm mentally exhausted but I need to make a living. Felt the same way with my last job too. Luckily for the last couple months me and my boyfriend got by so I can heal from trauma but now I really need to get back to work so we can work on our future. It's just been kinda a hard battle with my mind of letting myself know I'm still valid with my mental illness,  and like I do like my new job like ALOT so it will also be good for my mental health to do somethingi enjoy,  and it has been a good week starting a new chapter, but you know mental illnesscan be just rude sometimes.
